html: Full dataset

code.pseudocode: Collect the labelled examples the model could learn from. Keep the whole set together until the split is defined.
Shuffle the examples with a fixed random seed. The order is reproducible but no longer tied to how the data was collected.
code.python:
import random

rng = random.Random(7)
order = list(range(24))
rng.shuffle(order)
print(order[:5])

code.pseudocode: Take about 70% of the shuffled examples as the training set. Their targets will be used to learn parameters.
code.python:
order = list(range(24))  # shuffled positions from the previous step
n_train = int(24 * 0.70)
train_positions = order[:n_train]
print(len(train_positions))

code.pseudocode: Take about 15% as the validation set. These examples are kept out of training and are used to compare choices.
code.python:
order = list(range(24))  # shuffled positions from the previous step
n_train = int(24 * 0.70)
n_val = int(24 * 0.15)
val_positions = order[n_train:n_train + n_val]
print(len(val_positions))

code.pseudocode: Reserve the remaining examples as the test set. Do not look at them while developing the model.
code.python:
order = list(range(24))  # shuffled positions from the previous step
n_train = int(24 * 0.70)
n_val = int(24 * 0.15)
test_positions = order[n_train + n_val:]
print(len(test_positions))

code.pseudocode: Fit the model using only training examples. Its parameters change; validation and test examples are not used here.
code.python:
train_targets = [40, 50, 60]
model_value = sum(train_targets) / len(train_targets)  # learned from training data only
print(model_value)

steps.label: Train only on the training set

code.pseudocode: Score candidate models on the validation set. Keep the one that performs best there, and adjust settings if needed.
code.python:
train_targets = [40, 50, 60]
model_value = sum(train_targets) / len(train_targets)  # learned from training data only
val_targets = [55]
val_error = abs(model_value - val_targets[0])
print(val_error)

code.pseudocode: After every choice is fixed, measure performance once on the test set. This is the number reported as the estimate.
code.python:
train_targets = [40, 50, 60]
model_value = sum(train_targets) / len(train_targets)  # fixed before the test set is used
test_targets = [70]
final_error = abs(model_value - test_targets[0])
print(final_error)

steps.label: Evaluate once on the test set
